chunks: From him, from Husayn ibn Hashim, from Ibn Muskan, from Abi Basir, who said:

Abu Abdillah عليه السلام said to me: Indeed, the one bereft of his family and wealth is the one who neglects the salat of al-'Asr. I said: What is al-mawtur? He said: He will have neither family nor wealth in Paradise. I said: And what is neglecting it? He said: He leaves it until it turns yellow and sets.

key_terms.الْجَنَّةِ: Paradise, where the deprived person will have no family or wealth
key_terms.الْمَوْتُورَ: one who is bereft and deprived
key_terms.تَصْفَرَّ: to become yellow, referring to the sun near sunset
key_terms.تَضْيِيعُهَا: neglecting or wasting the prayer by delaying it improperly
key_terms.تَغِيبَ: to set, referring to the sun’s disappearance

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about delaying the salat of al-'Asr until sunset?
ai.summary: This hadith warns severely against neglecting the salat of al-'Asr by describing such a person as deprived of family and wealth in Paradise. It explains that neglecting it means delaying it until the sun yellows and sets, highlighting the importance of performing the prayer within its proper time.
